65795.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר. The speaker who commands light into being is the Creator introduced in Genesis 1:1, matching the source tag.

65796.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּרְא. The Creator sees that the light is good.

65797.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the Creator who names the light Day and the darkness Night. The existing source tag identifies this bearer as LORD@Gen.1.1.

65804.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּרְא. The Creator introduced in Genesis 1:1 sees that the vegetation is good.

65810.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּרְא. The Creator introduced in Genesis 1:1 sees that the work is good.

65814.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיְבָרֶךְ. The God who created the sea creatures and birds in Genesis 1:21 now blesses them.

65816.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר. The speaker is the God of Genesis 1:1, who here commands the land to bring forth living creatures.

65817.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּעַשׂ, identifying the Creator who made the land animals.

65818.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר. The speaker is the God who creates in Genesis 1, matching the existing source tag.

65823.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּרְא. The Creator surveys all that he has made, identifying him as the God introduced in Genesis 1:1.

66050.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיְכַל. The work he completed is the work of creation begun in Genesis 1:1, and the source tag identifies the same bearer.

66052.evidence: Yahweh is the personal name of the God who made the earth and the heavens, the creator already identified in Genesis 1:1.
God stands in apposition to Yahweh. Both words identify the same creator.

66053.evidence: יַהְוֶה names Yahweh as the subject of the verb ‘had caused it to rain.’
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה in ‘Yahweh God.’ Both designate the same subject of the singular verb הִמְטִיר.

66055.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the God who forms the man.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה and designates the same divine subject of וַיִּיצֶר.

66056.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the God who planted the garden.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה and designates the same God.
בְּעֵדֶן identifies Eden as the place where Yahweh God planted the garden for the man he had formed.

66057.evidence: יַהְוֶה names Yahweh, who caused the trees to grow from the ground.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they identify the single subject of וַיַּצְמַח.

66058.evidence: The river flows from Eden to water the garden planted in Eden in Gen.2.8. The source tag identifies the same place.

66059.evidence: The verse names Pishon as the first of the four river branches and identifies it by its course around Havilah.
The phrase “land of Havilah” names the territory around which the Pishon flows and where the gold is. The source tag identifies this place with the Genesis 2:11 bearer.

66061.evidence: Gihon is explicitly named as the second river in the Eden account.
The phrase “land of Cush” identifies Cush as the territory around which the Gihon flows.

66062.evidence: The naming clause gives חִדֶּקֶל as the name of the third river.
The phrase קִדְמַת אַשּׁוּר places the Tigris east of Asshur. This geographical use supports the tagged place, whether the reference is to the city or its territory.
The closing clause identifies פְרָת as the fourth river.

66063.evidence: Yahweh names the God who takes the man and places him in the garden.
God stands in apposition to Yahweh and designates the same divine subject.

66064.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the speaker who commands the man.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה and designates the same speaker.

66066.evidence: Yahweh is the personal name of the speaker, whom the text calls Yahweh God. He promises to make a helper for the man and brings the woman to him in Gen.2.22.

66068.evidence: וּלְאָדָם uses the personal name Adam without the article. It refers to the man who has just named the animals, and the source tag identifies him as Adam@Gen.2.19.

66069.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the God who causes the deep sleep to fall on the man.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they form the subject of the singular verb וַיַּפֵּל.

66070.evidence: יַהְוֶה explicitly names the subject of וַיִּבֶן. The source tags this name LORD@Gen.1.1.

66305.evidence: Yahweh is the personal name of the God who made the animals of the field, the same Yahweh God who brought the woman to the man in Genesis 2:22.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to Yahweh. Together they identify the maker of the animals as the subject of the singular verb עָשָׂה.
The serpent uses אֱלֹהִים for the speaker whose command about eating from the garden’s trees it questions. Genesis 2:16–17 identifies that speaker as Yahweh God.

66309.evidence: The singular participle יֹדֵעַ agrees with אֱלֹהִים. The serpent is speaking of the God who gave the command about the tree.
The serpent repeats אֱלֹהִים with the comparative prefix כֵּ־, saying the hearers will be like the God just mentioned in their knowledge of good and evil.

66312.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the God whom the man and his wife hear walking in the garden, the same Yahweh who brought the woman to the man in Genesis 2:22.
In יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, אֱלֹהִים designates Yahweh as God. The singular participle מִתְהַלֵּךְ describes him walking about.
The repeated name יַהְוֶה identifies the one from whom the couple hides as the same Yahweh they have just heard.
אֱלֹהִים again stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה and designates the God from whose presence the couple hides.

66321.evidence: The form לְאָדָם lacks the definite article. God addresses Adam as the husband who listened to his wife and ate from the forbidden tree, matching the existing person tag.

66324.evidence: The man explicitly gives his wife the name חַוָּה (Eve). The verse identifies her as the mother of all the living.

66325.evidence: יַהְוֶה names Yahweh, the God who makes the tunics and clothes Adam and his wife.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה in ‘Yahweh God.’ Both words identify the same singular subject, and both carry the same divine source tag.
לְאָדָם names Adam as a recipient alongside his wife, whom he named Eve in the preceding verse. This identifies the bearer as Eve’s husband.

66327.evidence: Yahweh is the personal name in ‘Yahweh God.’ The God who brought the woman to the man in Genesis 2:22 now sends the man out of the garden.
The man leaves the garden that Yahweh God planted in Eden in Genesis 2:8. The source tag identifies the same place.

66328.evidence: The phrase גַן עֵדֶן identifies the garden planted in Eden in Genesis 2:8. The cherubim are stationed east of that garden.

66561.evidence: The verse names Eve as the man's wife and identifies her as Cain's mother.
Cain is the name of the son Eve bears in this verse.
Eve explicitly names Yahweh, the same God who brought the woman to the man in Genesis 2:22.

66562.evidence: Abel is named as the brother of Cain, whom Eve bore in the preceding verse.
The repeated name identifies the same brother as a keeper of flocks.
Cain, Eve’s son named in Genesis 4:1, is paired with his brother Abel as the one who tills the soil.

66563.evidence: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve named in Genesis 4:1, tills the ground in Genesis 4:2 and brings some of its produce here.
The prefixed לַ־ marks Yahweh as the recipient of Cain’s offering. Eve uses the same divine name at Cain’s birth in Genesis 4:1.

66564.evidence: The giver brings firstborn from his flock, identifying him as Abel, the keeper of sheep and brother of Cain introduced in Genesis 4:2.

Yahweh looks on Abel and on his offering, naming the same Abel who brought the firstborn earlier in the verse.

66569.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the speaker who asks Cain about Abel. The LORD source tag identifies the same God as the earlier Yahweh proposal.
Yahweh addresses Cain and calls Abel his brother, identifying the son born to Eve in Genesis 4:1.
“Your brother” identifies Abel as the brother of Cain introduced in Genesis 4:2.

66573.evidence: The speaker is Eve’s son Cain, Abel’s brother, responding to the sentence Yahweh has just pronounced on him for killing Abel.
Cain addresses יַהְוֶה, the God who has just pronounced his sentence. The LORD source tag identifies the same God as the earlier Yahweh proposal.

66576.evidence: The Cain who leaves here is Eve’s son and Abel’s brother, whom Yahweh addressed after Abel’s death.
The divine name identifies the God who addressed Cain and whose presence Cain now leaves. The source tag LORD refers to the same bearer as the earlier Yahweh proposal.
The phrase “in the land of Nod” names the territory where Cain settled and locates it east of Eden.
“East of Eden” locates Nod relative to the Eden where Yahweh God planted the garden in Genesis 2:8.

66578.evidence: Irad is born to this Enoch, whom the preceding verse identifies as Cain’s son.

Enoch’s son Irad is named again as the father of Mehujael.
Irad fathers the child named Mehujael.
The variant spelling names Irad’s son again as the father of Methushael.
Mehujael fathers the child named Methushael.
Mehujael’s son Methushael is named again as the father of Lamech.
The final clause identifies Lamech as Methushael’s son in Cain’s line.

66580.evidence: Genesis 4:19 names Adah as one of Lamech’s wives. Here she bears Jabal.
Jabal is the son Adah bears here. The verse calls him the father of those who live in tents and keep livestock.

66581.evidence: The verse names Jabal’s brother Jubal and identifies him as the father of those who play the lyre and pipe. The source tag at position 2 identifies the same musician.

66583.evidence: The speaker addresses his wives Adah and Zillah, the pair named in Genesis 4:19.
Lamech addresses Adah alongside Zillah as one of his wives, matching Genesis 4:19.
Lamech addresses Zillah alongside Adah as one of his wives, matching Genesis 4:19.
The speaker calls Adah and Zillah “wives of Lamech,” repeating his own name.

66819.evidence: Adam is the father who names his son Seth, matching the Adam who fathered Seth with Eve in Genesis 4:25.

66821.evidence: Genesis 5 records the 930-year lifespan of Adam, the father of Seth. The source tag identifies the same person.

66822.evidence: Seth fathers Enosh here, matching Adam and Eve’s son Seth, whose son is named Enosh in Genesis 4:26.
Enosh is the son Seth fathers here, the same father and son named in Genesis 4:26.

66825.evidence: The verse names Enosh as Kenan’s father, matching Seth’s son in the Genesis genealogy.
The verse names Kenan as the son Enosh fathered at age ninety.

66828.evidence: Kenan, named as Enosh’s son in Genesis 5:9, is seventy when he fathers Mahalalel here.
Here Mahalalel is Kenan’s son in the pre-Flood genealogy. The Mahalalel of Nehemiah 11:4 is named as Shephatiah’s father.

66831.evidence: Kenan’s son, introduced in Genesis 5:12, is sixty-five when he fathers Jared here. The source tag agrees.
The verse names Jared as Mahalalel’s son in the genealogy before the Flood. His parentage distinguishes him from Jered son of Mered in 1 Chronicles 4:18. The source tag agrees.

66834.evidence: Genesis 5:15 names Jared as Mahalalel’s son. Here Jared fathers Enoch, matching the source tag.

66837.evidence: This Enoch fathers Methuselah, identifying him as Jared’s son in Genesis 5:18.
Methuselah is named as the son whom Enoch fathered at age sixty-five.

66839.evidence: This verse totals the lifespan of the Enoch whom Jared fathered in Genesis 5:18 and who fathered Methuselah in Genesis 5:21. The source tag identifies the same bearer.

66841.evidence: Methuselah, the son of Enoch named in Genesis 5:21, fathers Lamech at age 187.
This verse names Methuselah as Lamech’s father. The Lamech in Genesis 4:18 is the son of Methushael.

66843.evidence: This verse closes the lifespan of Enoch’s son Methuselah, introduced in Genesis 5:21 and named as Lamech’s father in Genesis 5:25. The source tag identifies the same bearer.

66844.evidence: Genesis 5:25 identifies this Lamech as Methuselah’s son, and 5:29 names his son Noah. The Lamech of Genesis 4:18 is Methushael’s son.

66847.evidence: Genesis 5:25 identifies Lamech as Methuselah’s son, and Genesis 5:28–30 identifies him as Noah’s father. This verse closes his lifespan at 777 years.

Japheth is the third son named in the list of sons Noah fathered.

67334.evidence: The verse gives Noah’s age at the flood, identifying him as Lamech’s son. The source tag agrees.

67337.evidence: The animals go to Noah at the ark, identifying Lamech’s son in the flood account.

67343.evidence: The creatures enter the ark to join Noah, the son of Lamech who survives the flood. The source tag identifies the same bearer.

67344.evidence: Yahweh is the personal name of the God who commanded Noah and then shut him in the ark. Both clauses carry the same source bearer tag, supporting reuse of the previously proposed Yahweh key.

67351.evidence: Noah survives the flood with those in the ark. This identifies the son of Lamech named in Genesis 5:29 and agrees with the source tag.

67590.evidence: The man who opens the ark’s window is Noah, the flood survivor and son of Lamech. The source tag identifies the same bearer.
